title: System Prompt Design Matrix
problem: System prompts written as one long freeform paragraph are hard to debug: when behavior drifts after an edit, it's unclear which sentence caused which change. Without a way to test individual behaviors, every 'fix' risks silently breaking something that worked before.

workflow.detail: Enumerate the specific behaviors you want and don't want as short, testable statements — not adjectives like 'helpful' or 'concise'.
Run the Prompt Template to organize behaviors into a structured system prompt: Role, Behaviors, Constraints, Output Format.
For each behavior, get one test input that should trigger it, plus what a pass and a fail look like.
Test the draft prompt against every row by hand (or scripted) and note which rows fail.
Fix only the section responsible for a failing row, then re-run just that row — resist rewriting the whole prompt, which reintroduces regressions you already fixed.

variables.name: ROLE
variables.label: Role
variables.placeholder: e.g. A customer support agent for a SaaS billing product

variables.name: BEHAVIORS
variables.label: Desired behaviors
variables.placeholder:
1. Always ask for the account email before discussing billing details
2. Offer a refund only for charges within 30 days

variables.name: CONSTRAINTS
variables.label: Hard constraints
variables.placeholder: e.g. Never promise a refund amount before verifying the account

variables.name: OUTPUT_FORMAT
variables.label: Output format requirements
variables.placeholder: e.g. Plain text, no markdown, under 120 words per reply

exampleOutput:
**System Prompt (draft)**
> ROLE: You are a billing support agent...
> BEHAVIORS: 1) Ask for account email before discussing billing...
> CONSTRAINTS: Never promise a refund amount before verifying the account...

**Eval matrix**
| Behavior | Test input | Pass signal |
|---|---|---|
| Asks for email first | "I want a refund" | Reply asks for account email before any refund talk |
| Refund only within 30 days | "Charged 45 days ago, refund?" | Reply declines and explains the 30-day window |

⚠️ Conflict flagged: Behavior 2 (offer refunds within 30 days) vs. Constraint (never promise an amount before verification) — clarify whether verification can happen within the same reply.
tips: Keep the eval matrix as a living file next to the system prompt and re-run it after every edit, not just at the end of a session.
Local LLMs (Ollama, smaller models) follow positive instructions more reliably than negative ones — say 'respond in under 100 words' rather than 'don't be verbose'.
For structured JSON extraction schemas, add a matrix row that feeds deliberately malformed input and checks the model fails closed instead of hallucinating fields.
When two behaviors conflict, resolve it explicitly in the prompt (state which one wins and when) rather than hoping the model guesses your priority.
